Proof read line by line; no step fails. d odd: S = all odds in [1,2d-1] (2i+d for i <= (d-1)/2, 2i-d otherwise), a complete residue system; E = {d+1+4i} + {4i+1-d} = {d+1,d+3,..,3d-1} = S+d, so G = L+d as sets. (L): x < o(x) forces o = x+d, x even <= d-1 (W_lo); x >= o+da forces x-da in {o, o+d}, giving T and W_hi; correct. (C): max L = da+d-1 is true (direct: o+d(a-1) <= 2d-1+da-d; the parenthetical reason given is roundabout but right), complement of G in [d+1,y-1] is d + (W_lo + T cap [1,da+d-1]) = odds in [d+2,2d-1] + W_hi, and [1,d] = odds <= d + W_lo, total H' + W; correct (the displayed union lists the pieces in a shuffled order but the sets are right). d even: S, E as stated, both complete residue systems; the residue case analyses for lengths and cells check out, including r = 0 (x = 0 excluded) and r odd impossible for z >= e+da. |W| = d-1 in both parities, s_i >= 1 so u >= 1, cells <= y-1. Corollary D(a^k) for a >= k-2 follows with d = k-1, a1 = a. referee:cutinduction:proof.detail: Read T1-T4 line by line; no step fails. T1: kept brackets = n-1-|R| edges on n-|R| labels inside a tree, so they form the tree T[S]; new length = l - #(shorter R-brackets) = rank among kept brackets, so lengths are 1..n-|R|-1 and order is kept; growth follows because (edges of G_k) intersect T[S] is connected (path argument is valid). Converse is the same count read backwards. T2: the count n-1-(|S|-1)=|R1|+|R2| correctly forces that no bracket is both an R1- and an R2-bracket; (1) and (2) for the image follow. T3: local confluence from T2 with singletons (needs n>=4, stated), n=3 handled by hand (I checked both placements), Newman applies. T4: the chain staircase => all leaves clean => leaf end of bracket 1 clean => staircase is complete; the last step relies on README Lemma 8 and Theorem 9 (both marked proved in the repo), and the re-opening argument (p_{k+1}=q_k, bracket 2 = {L-1,L+1}, p_1 in {L-1,L}) is correct. Minor unstated but one-line items, not gaps: (i) the parenthetical in T2 'so the union is clean' needs the sentence that a kept bracket jumps #R1+#R2 labels = shorter R1-brackets + shorter R2-brackets (disjointness); (ii) T3's identification of 'peelable' with 'closure of Lemma 8 insertion from K2' uses that a Lemma-8 insertion yielding a growth placement is exactly the inverse of a clean-leaf deletion (true by Lemma 8's iff plus T1); (iii) the |R|=1 remark needs n>=3. Statement is not stronger than what is proved. Independent brute force from the definitions (t_check.py, my own code): growth counts 2,4,12,32,116,412,1764,7888 for n=3..10; over ALL label sets R, n<=10: 0 violations of T1, T1-converse, T2 (incl. union clean), T3 (set of terminal placements over all deletion orders is a singleton), T4; staircases = 2^(n-2); n=9 gives 83,486 clean sets and 246,224 ordered disjoint clean pairs, exactly as claimed; non-order-preserving growth restrictions 16 at n=7 as claimed. The window lemma holds, and the quoted numbers reproduce, but two parts of the statement are stronger than the evidence. LEMMA: correct but nearly a tautology. 'Placed' and 'later' are process words; read as 'any edge of length l < L', the child sits at distance l <= L-1 from y, and the endpoint bounds are immediate. The proof is fine line by line. NUMBERS: every success row quoted for n = 1000 matches run_grid.log (I extracted all 13 types x 3 policies); 156/156 cells are 0/100 at eps = 0 and 156/156 are 100/100 at eps = 100%; there are 0 verification failures; the policy-6 least-slack medians match run_extra.log. It should read as a tendency with its setting stated. (b) says the least slack 'is linear in n', and the proof field ends 'This is why the needed slack is a constant fraction of n and not o(n) for this process'. That is asserted as fact from four sizes (200..2000) of a non-monotone statistic plus an argument the claimant itself labels heuristic. The data are consistent with linear growth (my extra n = 4000 runs: policy 6 median 320, ratio 0.080; policy 1 mean 585, ratio 0.146) but do not exclude o(n). It should read 'roughly proportional to n for 200 <= n <= 2000 (4000)', and the not-o(n) sentence should be marked as conjecture. (a) is correct as worded ('tried', centroid root). At eps = 0 the process allows no skipped length at all, so 0/100 means only that a random no-backtrack growth build fails; a star rooted at its centre would succeed trivially and was not among the types tried.

The proof is complete; I checked every step and found no gap. (1) me and mo are distinct values in 0..n-1, so me + mo <= 2n-3 and N <= 2n-2; the odd class is non-empty for n >= 2. (2) Even labels lie in [1, 1+me]; odd labels are N+1-sigma with 1 <= sigma <= mo, so they lie in [2+me, N]; the two ranges are disjoint and sigma is injective within each class. (3) Every edge joins opposite parities, so its length is N - sigma(p) - sigma(c) >= N - me - mo = 1. (4) BFS queue order gives sigma(c) < sigma(c') => sigma(par c) <= sigma(par c'), so s(c) = sigma(c) + sigma(par c) is strictly increasing in sigma(c) and all lengths are distinct. (5) For p -> c -> c': sigma(c') > sigma(c) > sigma(p) gives s(c') > s(c), so the lower edge is strictly shorter. (6) f(r) = 1. The statement is no stronger than what is proved; the argument works for any order of children in the queue. Independent check (bfs_ref.py, run_bfs_ref.log): all free trees on n = 2..12, every root, 3 queue orders (33,015 runs), plus 1,200 random rooted trees with 13 <= n <= 400, all pass, including the intermediate proof facts (the length formula and the monotonicity of s). The bound N = 2n-2 is attained exactly by a path rooted at an end. The claimant's bfs_bound_check.py reproduces its stated output (126,125 and 14,201 rooted trees, largest N/n 1.993). Minor points: the closing 'gap to claim 1' should refer to the slack-1 Observation, which is claim 0 in this numbering; 'in the style of classical 2n-type labelings' gives no citation, but no novelty is claimed.

(2) S_0 and facts (i)-(iv) follow from S_{r-1}; the twice/once/never rule (j>J, j=J, j<J, with j=r+1 sliding twice iff r<=a-2) follows from comparing min(T_j,2r+3-2j) with min(T_j,2r+5-2j); caps of br1 give (a) iff 2r<=a and (c) iff 2r<a. (3) Every named path: each edge is present at that moment (the descending order of j guarantees bracket 2j+1 has already moved to {q,R+2} and bracket 2j-3 has not moved; {1,R+2} exists because r<=a-2 whenever it is used; in (c) 2r<a and r>=1 give r<=a-2), vertices are distinct, and the sliding bracket is on the path. The three cases of (d) are exhaustive and disjoint (2a-2r is even in 4..2r exactly in the third case). Tail uses bracket k-1 at 2 and k+1 at 1, both true. Unstated but harmless: paths must be simple (they are); for j=2 with J=2 the remark br1={R-1,R} still holds since 2r=a means step (a) ran. 'Route is nearly forced' is informal, not a claim. Lemma F: proof is complete (new feet x+-1, y+-1; one equals the leaf l only if k=1, and then the other new foot differs from l and lies in the rest). Both feet cannot be leaves for n>=3, so 'the leaf foot' is well defined. Theorem I: conclusion correct, with one small slip in the proof text: for br k, 3<=k<=n-3, the piece of k+1 is listed as '{k+1}, or {n-3,n-1} (k = n-4), or {4,3} in P' (k = 3)'. At n=7 in P' the cases k=3 and k=n-4 coincide and the piece is {3,4,6}, which is none of the three listed sets. The conclusion is unaffected (2 and k+2=5 are not in {3,4,6}), so this is a wording gap, not a failing step.
